2.
Both the claimant as well as the BMTC are in appeal challenging the quantum of compensation.
3. The BMTC contends that the attribution of negligence entirely on the driver of the BMTC bus was incorrect.
It is also contended that the sums awarded by the Tribunal are excessive.

An argument is also advanced that the additional documents that are produced along with the present appeal indicating further medical treatment are not relatable to the accident and therefore, they cannot be considered.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimant, on the other hand, contends that the sums awarded by the Tribunal are on the lower side and that the discharge summary that has now been produced indicates that the claimant had sustained injuries in the accident and he therefore would be entitled to higher compensation.
It is also argued that disability assessed at 8% is on the lower side and the sums awarded under the various heads are on the lower side.

5. As far as negligence is concerned, the driver of the bus has stated that the claimant hit his bus on the front right end bumper and this was due to rash and negligent driving by the claimant himself.

6. It is not in dispute that the BMTC bus driver was charge-sheeted by the Police and this by itself indicates that even according to the Police, the driver of the BMTC bus was responsible for the accident.

The manner in which the BMTC bus driver has described the occurrence of the accident would itself indicate that the driver of the bus had a clear vision of the road and ought to have taken adequate steps to avoid collision.
In this view of the matter, I find no reason to disturb the finding of the Tribunal that the driver of the BMTC bus alone was responsible for the accident.
7. The Tribunal has noticed the evidence of the doctor, who was examined and it has assessed the disability at 8% to the whole body.
However, the doctor who was examined was not the treated doctor and he has assessed the disability at 25% to the whole body.
8. His evidence indicates that the claimant had suffered a fracture of right femur, fracture of left clavicle and fracture of 6th and 7th ribs.
In my view, these factors cannot lead to an inference that the claimant had suffered 25% disability to the whole body.
9. The claimant had produced a discharge summary issued by Vydehi Hospital where he had been initially admitted.
The said discharge summary indicates that the claimant was admitted with trauma to his right forehead, right leg, right thigh, right side abdomen and he was admitted and treated at the hospital.

The discharge summary indicates that the diagnosis was with poly- trauma fracture leg, diaphragmatic tear, lacerated liver and lung, with diaphragmatic injury with closed displaced right femur shaft fracture, left clavicle fracture and right zygomatic fracture.
This indicated in the discharge summary that he was subjected to a surgical procedure and was actually put on a mechanical ventilator initially.
It is also noticed that the claimant was suffering from a discharge of puss from the thoracotomy wound.

10. Along with this appeal, an application for additional evidence is filed, which indicates that the claimant admitted himself to the Vydehi hospital with a complaint of discharging sinus from post-Thoracotomy scar since past three years.

The discharge summary indicates that the claimant had developed wound discharge from the thoracotomy scar and initially, it was a thick yellowish scanty discharge, but it had progressed to copious, watery, yellowish, foul smelling, non-blood tinged discharge.
The discharge summary also indicates that he underwent wire removal surgery under local anesthesia and was hospitalised from 22.09.2020 to 23.09.2020 and thereafter, from 12.11.2020 to 15.11.2020.

sentences.text: The medical bills that are produced also indicates that he had spent a sum of Rs.1,21,244/-.

This discharge summary indicates that even three years after the accident, the claimant was still suffering from a discharge from the Thorocotamy scar that he had undergone in the year 2017 and this indicates that there has been a lasting effect on his health.
In my view, therefore, it would be appropriate to treat the whole body disability of the claimant at 15% as against 8% determined by the Tribunal.
12. There is no evidence to indicate the actual income earned by the claimant.
It would therefore be appropriate to adopt the sum of Rs.11,000/- fixed by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in respect of the accidents of the year 2017.

13. As the claimant was aged 35 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121,
a multiplier of '16' would have to be applied.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.3,16,800/- (Rs.11,000/- x 12 x '16' x 15%) towards loss of future earnings due to disability.
14. The sum of Rs.1,89,834/- awarded as medical expenses by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence, does not call for modification and hence confirmed.
15. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses.

Since the claimant has produced bills indicating that he has incurred further sum of Rs.1,21,244/-, it would be appropriate to increase the sum awarded towards future medical expenses to a sum of Rs.1,21,244/-
apart from Rs.20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal earlier i.e., in all Rs.1,41,244/-.
16.

The Tribunal has taken the laid up period as two months and has awarded a sum of Rs.16,000/-
towards loss of income during laid up period.

In my view, since the claimant has been hospitalised on two occasions and had a continuous discharge, it would be appropriate to treat the laid up period as six months and award a sum of Rs.66,000/- (Rs.11,000/- x 6 months).
- 10 - 17.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering and a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.

In my view, since the claimant had to undergo a surgery and was hospitalised for 65 days, it would be just and appropriate to award a sum of Rs.1,25,000/-
towards pain and suffering and a similar sum of Rs.1,25,000/- towards loss of amenities.
18. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards 'conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges'.

In my view, having regard to the length of the stay of the claimant in the hospital and that he had been hopitalised on three different occasions, the claimant would also be entitled to 'conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges' at Rs.50,000/- as against the sum of Rs.20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

19. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
